gap: No result ChatGPT got states that UGREEN's "48,000 mAh" is counted at 3.2 V LiFePO4 cells (153.6 Wh), so on the 3.6 V scale the 40,000 mAh rivals use it is about 42,700 mAh: 6.7% more energy than a 144 Wh Cuktech 30, not 20%, at about 46% more weight; and that every "300 W" or "140 W" bank in this size gives one laptop the same 140 W.
standout_why: Compared against powerbanks.fyi/best/laptop-power-banks (cited), Macworld's MacBook roundup and its UGREEN review, and best-batteries.com's high-capacity page. powerbanks.fyi lists 144 Wh / 1,130 g for the Cuktech 30 and 153.6 Wh / 1,637 g for the UGREEN, but gives no cell voltage, no per-port watts and no cycle life. Macworld gives 153.6 Wh, 140 W fastest port and 1.8 MacBook Pro charges, but no chemistry or cycle life. best-batteries gives LiFePO4 and 3,000 cycles, but no Wh for the UGREEN. So the raw pieces are scattered across rivals and none does the conversion or the same-scale comparison. Not checked: Tom's Guide (cited; its article body would not load), Wired, solargenadvisor, carryonworkspace. One of them may have part of this.
decides: It reframes the pick rather than flipping it. The UGREEN 48,000 mAh should be sold as the long-life desk and camping bank (3,000 cycles to 80%, maker claim), not as "20% more capacity". Its real energy lead over a 40,000 mAh bank is about 4-7%, and it weighs about 0.5 kg more than the Cuktech 30. For one laptop, the 300 W label adds nothing over a 140 W bank, because the most one port gives is 140 W on the UGREEN and on the Cuktech 30. The 300 W only matters for two or three laptops at once (UGREEN: 100 W on each of three USB-C). That supports a split: the UGREEN for longevity and several laptops at a desk, a lighter 40,000 mAh 140 W bank (the AOHi Starship) when it gets carried. The Cuktech 30 is unavailable on its maker's store today.

findings.label: Stated capacity and energy
findings.source_title: Best laptop power banks for Apple MacBook 2026 | Macworld
findings.note: Macworld's spec line: 'Battery capacity: 48000mAh (153.6Wh)'. powerbanks.fyi shows the same 153.6 Wh. UGREEN's US page returned HTTP 429 on every attempt today, so this is a reviewer's figure, not the maker's.

findings.label: Voltage the mAh figure is counted at (derived)
findings.value: 3.2 V per cell; equal to about 42,700 mAh at 3.6 V or about 41,500 mAh at 3.7 V
findings.source_title: Best laptop power banks for Apple MacBook 2026 | Macworld
findings.note: Our arithmetic: 153.6 Wh ÷ 48 Ah = 3.20 V, the nominal LiFePO4 voltage. 153.6 ÷ 3.6 = 42.67 Ah; 153.6 ÷ 3.7 = 41.5 Ah. The LiFePO4 chemistry is sourced separately (Android Central, best-batteries).

findings.label: Chemistry and cycle life (maker claim, as reported)
findings.source_title: UGREEN 300W 48000mAh Power Bank review | Android Central (Harish Jonnalagadda, 24 June 2024)
findings.note: Android Central reports it as UGREEN's claim. best-batteries.com's high-capacity page also lists LiFePO4 and 3,000 cycles (read 2026-11-26). No cycle-life figure turned up for the Cuktech 30, AOHi Starship 40K or Techsmarter, so there is nothing to normalise them against.

findings.label: Ports: one port, and ports together
findings.value: 1× USB-C 140 W (PD 3.1), 2× USB-C 100 W (PD 3.0), 2× USB-A 22.5 W; 300 W total; all three USB-C together give 100 W each
findings.source_title: Ugreen 48000mAh Portable Power Bank review: more power and ports than most | Macworld
findings.note: Port ratings are from Macworld's review, which also says 'you can't use all three USB-C ports at full power'. The 100 W each split is from Android Central's review (same URL as the cycle-life finding, read 2026-11-26). So 300 W means 3 × 100 W; one laptop gets 140 W at most.

findings.label: Recharge input and time
findings.value: 140 W input; about 1.5 hours (Macworld); just over 100 minutes (Android Central)
findings.source_title: Ugreen 48000mAh Portable Power Bank review | Macworld
findings.note: Both are reviewer measurements from a 140 W charger.

findings.label: Delivered capacity (reviewer measured)
findings.value: 1.8 charges of a 14-inch M2 MacBook Pro
findings.source_title: Best laptop power banks for Apple MacBook 2026 | Macworld
findings.note: Macworld: 'we recharged a 14-inch M2 MacBook Pro 1.8 times'. Separately, Android Central (Harish Jonnalagadda) reports about 55% efficiency counted in mAh: 8,500 mAh of the bank's reading used to fill a 4,500 mAh phone. That is what a 3.2 V mAh figure feeding 3.85 V phone cells looks like. This came through a page summary, so check the wording before quoting.

findings.label: Normalised comparison: energy against the mAh label
findings.value: UGREEN's '48,000 mAh' is +20% on the label against a 40,000 mAh bank, but +6.7% in energy against the Cuktech 30 (153.6 vs 144 Wh), for about +45% weight (1,637 vs 1,130 g)
findings.note: Our arithmetic from the Wh and gram figures on that page: 153.6 ÷ 144 = 1.067; 1,637 ÷ 1,130 = 1.449. The cause is LiFePO4 cells at 3.2 V against 3.6 V lithium-ion. The footnote for the table: compare Wh, not mAh.

findings.label: Normalised comparison: watts to one laptop
findings.value: 140 W is the most one USB-C port gives on both the UGREEN 48K '300 W' and the Cuktech 30 '300 W'
findings.source_title: Ugreen 48000mAh Portable Power Bank review | Macworld
findings.note: UGREEN's figure is from Macworld; the Cuktech figure is from ChargerLAB's teardown (USB-C2 28 V 5 A). The total-output number on the box is the sum across ports and does not charge one laptop faster. The AOHi is labelled by its single-port figure, 140 W.
